candidates.name: THE WOLLEMI PINE
candidates.headline: A tree from an ancient lineage was hiding in an Australian gorge.
candidates.why_survives: An isolated wild population persisted; propagation now also keeps the species in botanic gardens.
candidates.where_now: Wild trees survive in Wollemi National Park, with cultivated trees in gardens worldwide.
candidates.note: Critically endangered. Avoid treating the modern species as unchanged since the dinosaurs or using an undated population count.

candidates.name: VINYL RECORDS
candidates.headline: The record never stopped turning. It found another audience.
candidates.why_survives: A continuing market for physical records supports new pressings alongside digital listening.
candidates.where_now: RIAA reports continued US vinyl revenue growth in its 2025 recorded-music report.
candidates.note: The cited report covers the US market in 2025; revenue growth does not establish worldwide dominance or explain all buying motives.

candidates.name: RSS
candidates.headline: The feed survived the reader. The open web kept sending updates.
candidates.why_survives: Feed readers can still collect new articles directly from sites without a social-media timeline.
candidates.where_now: Thunderbird continues to document built-in support for RSS and Atom subscriptions.
candidates.note: RSS is a family of feed formats, not a single discontinued product. The support article establishes ongoing functionality, not usage share.

candidates.name: LONDON GAS LAMPS
candidates.headline: Electric light took over. Some London streets still glow with gas.
candidates.why_survives: Heritage protection and specialist maintenance preserve surviving gas-powered street lights.
candidates.where_now: Working gas lamps remain in London, including protected examples in Covent Garden.
candidates.note: Source published in February 2024; UK Parliament confirms further protection in April 2025. No current lamp count is claimed. Listing is not a guarantee that every lamp operates nightly. Supporting source: https://questions-statements.parliament.uk/written-questions/detail/2025-03-24/HL6077

candidates.name: THE SOLENT HOVERCRAFT
candidates.headline: The future of transport became a daily crossing that never went away.
candidates.why_survives: Its ability to cross shallow water and land directly on shore suits the tidal beaches at Ryde.
candidates.where_now: Hovertravel still carries passengers between Southsea and Ryde on the Isle of Wight.
candidates.note: This is a scheduled passenger service, not the retired cross-Channel car hovercraft. Avoid world-only claims: the operator has used inconsistent wording, and other services exist. Weather can interrupt crossings.

candidates.name: DOT-MATRIX PRINTERS
candidates.headline: The office went quiet. Somewhere, a print head is still rattling.
candidates.why_survives: Impact printing handles multipart forms; legacy-system compatibility keeps it useful for specialist work.
candidates.where_now: Epson still lists impact dot-matrix printers for continuous paper and multipart forms.
candidates.note: Manufacturer listing establishes an ongoing product offering and supported functions, not worldwide sales volume. Survival explanation is an editorial inference from the documented multipart-form and legacy integration features.

candidates.name: INTERNET RELAY CHAT
candidates.headline: Before the chat apps, there were channels. People are still in them.
candidates.why_survives: Volunteer-run networks and open-source project communities continue to use the IRC protocol.
candidates.where_now: Libera Chat operates an IRC network for free software and collaborative projects.
candidates.note: IRC is a protocol, not one surviving application. Libera Chat is a current example, not a claim that every historic IRC network survives or that usage is growing. Supporting sources: https://libera.chat/ and https://libera.chat/about/

candidates.name: ATLANTIC HORSESHOE CRABS
candidates.headline: An ancient body plan still leaves tracks on Atlantic beaches.
candidates.why_survives: Coastal habitat, spawning beaches and managed harvest help sustain surviving populations.
candidates.where_now: Atlantic horseshoe crabs still spawn on US shores, including Delaware Bay.
candidates.note: Ancient lineage does not mean the modern species is unchanged for hundreds of millions of years. They are not true crabs. Conservation status varies by region; avoid implying that survival means secure populations. Habitat and harvest context: https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/feature-story/horseshoe-crabs-managing-resource-birds-bait-and-blood
